tagline: New Delhi, India · Microsculptor & thread artist
intro: Yuvraj Singh Nain sculpts miniature forms into the tips of pencils and builds portraits from thread wound across nails. Each piece is made by hand, one at a time, for collectors around the world.

honours.text: Records registered with the India Book of Records
International commissions delivered to collectors abroad
celebrities shared on their Instagram profiles

micro_heading: A sculpture smaller than a your fingertip .
micro_text: Working under magnification, Yuvraj carves letters, figures and symbols directly into the graphite tip of an ordinary pencil. The material is brittle and forgives nothing: one slip and the work is lost.
thread_heading: Faces that appear from thousands of lines.
thread_text: Hundreds of nails are set into a board, then thread is wound from nail to nail, line over line, until a likeness emerges. Up close it is pure geometry; step back and a person looks out at you.
contact_text: Tell me what you have in mind: a portrait of someone you love, a name carved in graphite, a gift no one else will have.
about_bio:
I’m Yuvraj Singh Nain, an artist fascinated by the idea of creating something extraordinary out of the smallest things. My journey lies at the intersection of art, engineering, and curiosity. After completing my B.Tech in Mechatronics from MIT Manipal, I’m currently pursuing an LL.B. at the University of Delhi, while continuing to explore new possibilities through my art.

I create microsculptures by carving intricate designs on pencil tips, turning something as ordinary as a pencil into a tiny canvas. I also create thread portraits using thousands of nails and meters of fine thread, where every strand plays a part in bringing a face to life.

With three registered records in the India Book of Records and my artwork reaching collectors internationally, I continue to challenge myself to create things that seem almost impossible at first glance.

For me, art is about patience, experimentation, and the joy of making the impossible possible. Whether it’s a sculpture smaller than a fingertip or a portrait built from thousands of Nails and a continuous thread, I want every piece to make people pause, look closer, and see the extraordinary in the ordinary.
